title: The Stone That Moved

plate.narration: In the Red Sky Foothills, a broad stone stands beside a pale hollow in the grass. The stone is still. The hollow is empty. There is plenty here to look at carefully.

goal.text: Find what moved and get the neighbors safely past the stone.

steps.label: Get the water jars to the keepers
Teach a neighbor the safe road

stone.narration: Three dragonling keepers stare at a stone beside an empty hollow. "Our counting stone moved overnight," says one. "Now the water cart cannot make its turn. Help us find what moved, and get the neighbors safely past it." Pip Thistledown, a young manticore Riftseeker, measures the hollow with his tail. A keeper hands him a cord. "Try something that does not twitch."

marks.narration: The stone shows a carved mountain throwing sparks. "An eruption," says a keeper. "Our oldest counts disagree about when." One stroke is chipped. The hollow fits the stone exactly, but nothing dragged it there. Pip writes that down before his tail can add anything.

lesson.narration: Seren Wisp, the kitsune from the glacier, sits down beside Pip with her own notes. Seren asks you to hum the hall note and listen for an answer. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune. Answering never changes a rift's rules."

variants.text: Seren Wisp is here too, comparing notes with Pip. "Another moved place," she says, and asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before.

footprint.narration: A faint hum answers from beside the stone, then fades. The keepers bring two old drawings of the stone. One was drawn from the road, by the forked rock. One was drawn from the ridge. Their sight lines meet at the empty hollow. "That stone," says Pip, "is definitely not where we left it."

grass_test.narration: Wind combs the grass between the stone and the hollow. A dragged stone would leave a scrape. "Tell me when it lies still," says a keeper. Pip opens his mouth to guess, then wisely shuts it.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the grass lies still.

onSuccess.narration: The grass is untouched. Nothing dragged the stone.

onFailure.narration: A gust hides your first look. A keeper blocks the wind, and you look again. The grass is untouched.

onAssisted.narration: The grass is untouched. Nothing dragged the stone.

views.narration: You lay the road drawing beside the ridge drawing. A rock hidden from the road stands in plain view from the ridge. "Two honest drawings," says a keeper. "One very rude stone."

witness_result.narration: You mark the old hollow and today's stone. The eruption date stays a mystery. Then wheels squeak. The water cart has arrived. Its owner looks at the blocked turn, then at her jars. "Please tell me that stone moves back."

cart_plan.narration: The jars must reach the keepers' counting circle, below the turn, but the stone blocks the way. Build a short ramp and roll the loaded cart over: heavy work, but the ramp stays for tomorrow. Or carry the jars along the high path, then bring the empty cart down. Which plan?

ramp_setup.narration: A keeper lays two boards around the turn. Hold them steady while the cord goes under. Pip starts drawing a proud little flag on the ramp. The owner clears her throat. He draws the wheel tracks first.

interaction.cue: Hold the boards while the cord is tied.

onSuccess.narration: The ramp holds. Bring the cart across.

onFailure.narration: The ramp holds. Bring the cart across.

onAssisted.narration: The ramp holds. Bring the cart across.

braced_ramp.narration: Your thornguard braces the boards against the stones, so nobody else has to hold them. The cart owner pats a jar. "Your turn to be steady."

cart_balance.narration: The cart tips as the jars slosh. Keep it level across the ramp. One lid rattles like a tiny bell. Pip keeps his tail far from the spokes.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the loaded cart is level.

onSuccess.narration: The cart rolls over. The ramp will work again tomorrow.

onFailure.narration: The cart wobbles, then rolls over. The ramp will work again tomorrow.

onAssisted.narration: The cart rolls over. The ramp will work again tomorrow.

jar_relay.narration: Pass the sealed jars hand to hand along the high path, down to the counting circle. Pip offers to carry two at once. He looks at his tail and decides one is plenty.

interaction.cue: Catch the water jar, then pass it on.

onSuccess.narration: The jars reach the circle. Now the empty cart.

onFailure.narration: The jars reach the circle. Now the empty cart.

onAssisted.narration: The jars reach the circle. Now the empty cart.

empty_cart.narration: The empty cart is light enough to squeeze around the hollow. Guide its front wheel between two stones. "A jar would make a fine wheel stop," says Pip. "A broken jar," says the owner.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold to guide the wheel through the clear gap.

onSuccess.narration: The empty cart reaches the circle.

onFailure.narration: The wheel bumps a pebble. You move it and try again. The cart reaches the circle.

onAssisted.narration: The empty cart reaches the circle.

water_delivered.narration: Water reaches the counting circle, and the keepers fill their cups. Pip drinks too fast and hiccups so hard his tail jumps. The owner asks for one more thing: a warning, so nobody trusts the old turn.

camp.narration: You rest on a low stone. A keeper shares apple slices. Pip uses one to hold his drawing flat, then eats it, then wonders where his paperweight went. Two neighbors are coming: a walker from below the blind rise, and a cart from the upper road.

paperweight.narration: Pip holds the flapping page in one paw and his apple core in the other. The keepers have seen this before. How do you keep a drawing on a rock?

warning.narration: There is one big board for a warning and a few stones for a small one. Put the big sign below the blind rise, and walkers stop in time, but you must guide the cart. Put it above the turn, and carts can brake, but you must meet the walker. "Both neighbors are coming," Pip reminds you.

lower_sign.narration: Carry the big board down the dry path and tie it to the lower posts. Walkers will see it before the hollow. Above you, wheels begin to rattle.

interaction.cue: Catch the cord and pass it around the posts.

onSuccess.narration: The walker sees the sign and waits. Hurry up to the cart!

onFailure.narration: The cord slips, then holds. The walker waits. Hurry up to the cart!

onAssisted.narration: The walker sees the sign and waits. Hurry up to the cart!

upper_sign.narration: Set the big board well before the upper turn, so a cart has room to stop. Hold it while the corner is tied. Below the blind rise, the walker waves at the little stone arrow. She cannot see the hollow from there.

interaction.cue: Hold the sign while the corner is tied.

onSuccess.narration: The cart driver spots the sign and stops. Now go meet the walker.

onFailure.narration: The board tilts, then holds. The driver stops. Now go meet the walker.

onAssisted.narration: The cart driver spots the sign and stops. Now go meet the walker.

upper_cart.narration: Up here, the cart driver needs your signal. Call it when the front wheel reaches the keeper's white marker. Pip holds out his tail as an arrow. It points three ways at once. You use your hand.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the wheel reaches the turning marker.

onSuccess.narration: The driver takes the new turn and stops at the circle.

onFailure.narration: You call too early. The driver waits for your second call. The upper road needs a bigger sign.

onAssisted.narration: The driver takes the new turn and stops at the circle.

lower_neighbor.narration: Walk the neighbor past the blind rise the way you checked it. Tell her the landmarks in order, so she never has to guess what is behind the rise.

interaction.cue: Give the walker the route from below.
clues: The forked rock is the waiting place before the blind rise.
Go around the hollow after waiting, before joining the keepers.

onSuccess.narration: The walker reaches the circle and repeats the route back.

onFailure.narration: "Wait, which rock?" asks the walker. You walk it with her. The lower path needs a bigger sign.

onAssisted.narration: The walker reaches the circle and repeats the route back.

neighbor_result.narration: Both neighbors reach the counting circle. "Explain the turn back to me," Pip asks them. They can. Then a thin trickle of water starts down the ridge, toward the empty hollow.

variants.text: The lower road has the big sign. The upper road needs a bigger one.
The upper road has the big sign. The lower road needs a bigger one.

runoff.narration: The trickle will wash away the hollow's sharp edge, your best clue. A small drain could steer the water past it. Or spread gravel over the wet patch: a stronger road, but it buries the edge. What should last?

drain.narration: Steer the trickle past the sharp edge with a narrow board. Pip follows the water with his pencil, then drops it. He grabs it just before it sails away.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold to guide the trickle past the hollow.

onFailure.narration: Water washes one corner before the drain is set. That edge is lost.

gravel.narration: Level the gravel tray, then spread it on the wet patch. The sharp edge disappears underneath. "Better wheels," says a keeper. "A simpler drawing. We chose both."

interaction.cue: Level the gravel tray before spreading the load.

onSuccess.narration: The road is firm. Your drawing will use landmarks.

onFailure.narration: The road is firm. Your drawing will use landmarks.

onAssisted.narration: The road is firm. Your drawing will use landmarks.

evidence_decision.narration: Time to make the traveling page. The stone fits its hollow. The grass has no scrape. Nothing tells you the eruption's date. Pip dots in the chipped stroke and hands you the pencil. "Only what we saw."

exact_copy.narration: You copy the sharp outline. The chipped stroke stays dotted. Pip adds a tiny question mark. "Does it need a hat?" The keeper gives him a look.

landmark_copy.narration: A keeper draws the forked rock, the old hollow and today's stone. She leaves the lost edge blank and writes "from the road" on top.

motion.narration: Beside the stone, a fold in the air is narrowing. Seren holds two fingers apart, then pinches them closer. "Late travelers should know what that means." Nobody needs to cross it. You just need to show its time is running out.

motion_memory.narration: Seren taps a small slate. Each time, Pip marks the fold's width. Watch, then copy. A keeper lays a cord circle beside the marks. "This is a waiting place. Not a jumping place."

interaction.cue: Watch the width marks, then copy the change.

onSuccess.narration: Your marks show time running out.

onFailure.narration: Seren taps slowly, and you fix the marks. The fold is shrinking.

onAssisted.narration: Your marks show time running out.

motion_attuned.narration: Your starweaver hums back at the fold, the way Seren taught. The answering note makes its pulse easy to catch. It does not change the fold's rules.

interaction.cue: Use the answering note to catch the pulse in the wide gold band.

onSuccess.narration: The pulse and the edges agree. The fold is running out of time.

onFailure.narration: You miss one pulse, then catch the next. It is still shrinking.

onAssisted.narration: The pulse and the edges agree. The fold is running out of time.

stone_priority.narration: Pip holds up his traveling page. "Room for one big drawing." A road plan helps at the next moved crossing. The old marks let you compare this count with another stone. The keepers keep both here. Which do you carry?

route_copy.narration: The owner keeps a road plan for tomorrow. Pip tucks the traveling copy in his notebook. "Next time the road argues with the map, we have a starting point."

carving_copy.narration: A keeper copies the long stroke, the short strokes and the chip. Pip draws a dotted box beside them. "For the bit we do not know. Might need a bigger notebook."

rest.narration: Water jars stand beside full cups. The stone and its hollow are on the page, with no made-up date. Both neighbors know the new turn. "Thank you," says Pip. The road to Ashspan Bridge is open. The shrinking fold is another way on, but not for long.

variants.text: The keepers will add a larger upper sign for carts.
The keepers will add a larger lower warning for walkers.
Your reusable ramp stays for tomorrow.
Tomorrow's jars will need the passing line again.
The sharp edge is still there to measure.
The sharp edge is gone, and the missing detail stays missing.

paperweight_response_rock.narration: Pip puts the pebble on the corner. "A paperweight I cannot eat. Excellent."

paperweight_response_fold.narration: The page stays flat. Pip gives the folded corner a suspicious look, then nods.

paperweight_response_hold.narration: Pip finishes the line and thanks you. His tail tries to help. You move it off the ink.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
